question: All vaccines, including inactivated vaccines like IPV and subunit vaccines like Hepatitis B, must be stored between +2°C and +8°C; freezing is harmful to all of them.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct to mark this false. Freeze-sensitive vaccines include all adjuvanted inactivated vaccines (Hepatitis B, IPV, DPT). Live vaccines like OPV and varicella can be stored frozen. Freezing adjuvanted vaccines causes irreversible aggregation and potency loss — the shake test detects this.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false — some vaccines (e.g., varicella, OPV) can be stored frozen, and freezing inactivated and adjuvant-containing vaccines (such as Hepatitis B, DPT, IPV) can cause irreversible aggregation of adjuvant and loss of potency. However, the key nuance is that OPV can be frozen whereas inactivated vaccines must NOT be frozen.
